name: Stable cryptocurrencies

subjectOf.text: A currency that does not hold a stable store of value forces continual recalculation and renegotiation of contracts, so any future decentralized economy will require stable cryptocurrencies.
subjectOf.abstract: A fluctuating currency requires continual recalculation and renegotiation. Therefore, any future decentralized economy will require stable cryptocurrencies
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Vadhindran K. Rao, Stable Cryptocurrencies - First Order Principles (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3402701
scope_conditions: decentralized economies that rely on contracts denominated in the currency

subjectOf.text: Tether, like every other stable cryptocurrency project, remains afflicted with significant design challenges, even though its market capitalization and stability around one dollar give some support for stable cryptocurrencies' capacity to create market stability.
subjectOf.abstract: Like all other stable cryptocurrency projects, Tether is still afflicted with significant design challenges.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralization - Past, Present, and Future (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3411897
scope_conditions: as of the state of stable cryptocurrency design described in 2019

subjectOf.text: People will not enter into long term smart contracts without a stable currency to refer to, because the current level of cryptocurrency volatility does not lend itself to consumption.
subjectOf.abstract: Finally, people will not enter into a long-term smart contract unless they have a stable currency to refer to. The current level of volatility in cryptocurrencies does not lend itself to consumption.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralization - Past, Present, and Future (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3411897
scope_conditions: long duration smart contracts such as leases
